subject: Microbiology
subtopic: DNA viruses overview and DNA virus mnemonics
vignette: A 4-year-old girl is brought to the pediatrician for multiple small, flesh-colored, dome-shaped papules with central umbilication on the trunk and face. A scraping of one lesion shows large eosinophilic intracytoplasmic inclusions within keratinocytes. The child also has mild atopic dermatitis.
question: Which of the following best describes the causative agent?

options.text: An enveloped, linear dsDNA virus and the largest DNA virus, belonging to the poxvirus family
A naked, linear ssDNA virus that infects erythroid precursor cells
An enveloped, partially dsDNA, circular virus with reverse transcriptase activity
A naked, linear dsDNA virus that causes febrile pharyngitis and hemorrhagic cystitis
A naked, circular dsDNA virus that also causes cervical and oropharyngeal cancer

explanation_correct: The umbilicated flesh-colored papule containing molluscum bodies is molluscum contagiosum, caused by a poxvirus. Poxviruses are enveloped, linear dsDNA viruses and the largest DNA viruses, and they are the classic exception among DNA viruses in replicating in the cytoplasm rather than the nucleus. Smallpox, also a poxvirus, was eradicated worldwide with a live-attenuated vaccine.

explanation_incorrect.B: This describes parvovirus B19, the smallest DNA virus, which causes aplastic crisis in sickle cell disease and slapped-cheek rash rather than molluscum bodies.
explanation_incorrect.C: This describes hepatitis B virus, a hepadnavirus with reverse transcriptase; it does not cause skin papules.
explanation_incorrect.D: This describes adenovirus, which causes pharyngitis, hemorrhagic cystitis, and conjunctivitis but not molluscum contagiosum.
explanation_incorrect.E: This describes human papillomavirus, a naked circular dsDNA virus causing warts and cervical, anal, penile, and oropharyngeal cancer, not umbilicated molluscum lesions.

educationalObjective: Molluscum contagiosum is caused by a poxvirus, an enveloped linear dsDNA virus that is the largest DNA virus and the one DNA virus that replicates in the cytoplasm.

subject: Microbiology
subtopic: DNA viruses overview and DNA virus mnemonics
vignette: A 33-year-old man with untreated HIV infection (CD4 count 60/mm3) develops progressive clumsiness of the right arm and word-finding difficulty over 2 months. MRI shows nonenhancing demyelinating lesions in the subcortical white matter without mass effect. Brain biopsy reveals enlarged oligodendrocytes with glassy intranuclear inclusions.
question: Which of the following best describes the causative virus?

options.text: An enveloped, linear dsDNA herpesvirus that remains latent in B cells
A naked, linear ssDNA virus that infects endothelial cells
A positive-sense ssRNA flavivirus transmitted by mosquitoes
A negative-sense ssRNA paramyxovirus spread by respiratory droplets
A naked, circular dsDNA polyomavirus that also causes nephropathy in kidney transplant recipients

explanation_correct: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy is caused by JC virus, a polyomavirus: a naked, circular, dsDNA virus of the same family as BK virus. JC virus reactivates in immunocompromised patients such as those with advanced HIV and destroys oligodendrocytes, producing nonenhancing white matter demyelination. The mnemonic pair is JC: Junky Cerebrum and BK: Bad Kidney, since BK virus targets the kidney in transplant patients.

explanation_incorrect.A: This describes Epstein-Barr virus, which causes lymphomas, oral hairy leukoplakia, and mononucleosis but not PML.
explanation_incorrect.B: This describes parvovirus B19, the smallest DNA virus, which lyse RBC precursors and endothelial cells and does not demyelinate white matter.
explanation_incorrect.C: This describes a flavivirus such as West Nile or Zika; these cause meningoencephalitis or congenital malformations, not PML.
explanation_incorrect.D: This describes a paramyxovirus such as measles, which can cause SSPE, a dementing illness that follows wild-type measles years earlier and is not associated with CD4 depletion.

educationalObjective: JC virus is a naked circular dsDNA polyomavirus causing progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy in immunocompromised patients; BK virus, its relative, causes kidney disease in transplant recipients.

subject: Microbiology
subtopic: DNA viruses overview and DNA virus mnemonics
vignette: A 7-year-old boy with sickle cell disease presents with 2 days of fever, pallor, and fatigue. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin of 4 g/dL, reticulocytopenia, and a bone marrow aspirate with giant pronormoblasts but no erythroid maturation. Two weeks earlier he had a bright red rash on both cheeks.
question: Which of the following best explains his hematologic crisis?

options.text: Infection of B cells by a herpesvirus using CD21 as its receptor
Infection of endothelial cells by a flavivirus causing plasma leakage and hemoconcentration
Infection of CD4+ T cells by a retrovirus causing generalized marrow suppression
Destruction of infected RBCs by a mosquito-borne protozoan parasite
Infection of erythroid precursor cells by a naked ssDNA virus that uses the P antigen as its receptor

explanation_correct: Parvovirus B19 is the smallest DNA virus, a naked, linear ssDNA virus that enters erythroid precursors via the P antigen on RBCs. In patients with high RBC turnover such as sickle cell disease, infection causes transient pure red cell aplasia and an aplastic crisis. The preceding slapped-cheek rash in a child is erythema infectiosum, or fifth disease, the classic presentation in immunocompetent children.

explanation_incorrect.A: Epstein-Barr virus uses CD21 on B cells to cause mononucleosis and lymphoproliferation; it does not produce pure red cell aplasia or a slapped-cheek rash.
explanation_incorrect.B: Dengue virus produces thrombocytopenia and plasma leakage; it does not selectively destroy erythroid precursors.
explanation_incorrect.C: HIV depletes CD4+ T cells over years; it does not cause an acute reticulocytopenic crisis with giant pronormoblasts.
explanation_incorrect.D: Plasmodium falciparum invades RBCs and causes hemolysis, not parvovirus-like marrow arrest, and the presentation would follow mosquito exposure in an endemic area.

educationalObjective: Parvovirus B19 (naked ssDNA, smallest DNA virus, P antigen receptor) infects RBC precursors and causes aplastic crisis in chronic hemolytic anemias such as sickle cell disease.

subject: Microbiology
subtopic: DNA viruses overview and DNA virus mnemonics
vignette: A virology lecture presents a table of DNA virus families and asks students to predict which family represents the exception to the standard genome structure and which represents the exception to the standard intracellular site of replication.
question: Which of the following statements about DNA viruses is correct?

options.text: Adenoviruses are enveloped, circular dsDNA viruses that replicate in the nucleus
All DNA viruses have dsDNA genomes and replicate in the nucleus without exception
All DNA viruses are circular, except the poxviruses and papillomaviruses
Parvoviridae is the only ssDNA family and poxvirus is the only DNA virus replicating outside the nucleus
Hepadnaviruses are naked, linear dsDNA viruses that replicate in the cytoplasm

explanation_correct: DNA viruses have dsDNA genomes like our cells, with the single exception of Parvoviridae, which is ssDNA. All are linear except papillomavirus, polyomavirus, and hepadnavirus, which are circular. All are icosahedral and replicate in the nucleus except poxvirus, captured by the mnemonic Pox is out of the box (nucleus).

explanation_incorrect.A: Adenoviruses are naked and linear dsDNA viruses causing pharyngitis, hemorrhagic cystitis, and conjunctivitis.
explanation_incorrect.B: Parvoviridae is ssDNA, and poxvirus replicates in the cytoplasm, so both halves of this exception-free statement are wrong.
explanation_incorrect.C: Papillomavirus and polyomavirus are circular, not exceptions to circularity; the circular families are papilloma-, polyoma-, and hepadnavirus.
explanation_incorrect.E: Hepadnaviruses are enveloped, partially dsDNA and circular, and like other DNA viruses replicate in the nucleus; HBV also carries a reverse transcriptase.

educationalObjective: All DNA viruses are dsDNA except parvoviruses (ssDNA), all are linear except papilloma/polyoma/hepadnaviruses (circular), and all replicate in the nucleus except poxviruses.
